docs.task: How the session budget is enforced: where spend is summed, how the BudgetReached gate opens and is answered, and how YOLO treats it.

asks: Explain where session spend is summed.
Explain how the BudgetReached gate opens and how it is answered.
Explain how YOLO treats the BudgetReached gate.

data_flow.step: The setting `limits.session_budget_usd` (default 25.0, validated finite and not negative at save) lives in the workspace limits.
On each planning pass the runner reads it fresh into `PlanCtx.budget_usd`, with 0 mapped to None (no limit).

The planner builds spawn steps. Each `Step::Spawn` goes through `Planner::push`. Before the budget guard, push applies the awaiting-init hold (Rule O4) and the resume, continuation, and busy-conversation handling (Rules H2, P2, H5, H6, H7).

The guard computes `limit = budget + state.budget_raised` and `spent = state.spent_usd()`. `spent_usd` sums the cost of executions whose result is set, so running executions and judge calls are not in it.

If `spent >= limit`, the spawn is dropped. When `state.budget_gate` is None, one `Step::OpenGate` with `GatePayload::BudgetReached { spent_usd, budget_usd: limit }` is pushed (deduplicated by step key `gate:budget_reached:`). While a budget gate is open, further spawns are dropped silently.
The runner performs `Step::OpenGate` by appending `SessionEvent::GateOpened` with a new GateId. `Inner::append` stores, folds, and broadcasts it.
The fold records `budget_gate = Some(id)`. The gate's stage is `StageKind::Intake` and its kind string is `budget_reached`.

Under YOLO, `Planner::flows` iterates open gates and skips this one because `yolo_leaves_open` is true. If a `Step::YoloAnswer` were ever emitted, `perform_yolo` would find `yolo_plan` returning None and return without answering. A paused session plans nothing at all (Rule P1).

The user answers through `Engine::answer_gate`, which checks the gate is unanswered and that `validate_answer` accepts the answer. For BudgetReached only `GateAnswer::Choice` fits. It appends `GateAnswered { source: User, routed: answer_needs_route(..) }`. `answer_needs_route` is false for a budget answer, so no judge routes it.

The fold clears `budget_gate`. 'raise' adds to `budget_raised` (typed dollars, or the gate's limit with a floor of 1.0, plus any overshoot). Any other option sets `state.failed`, so the session ends as failed with 'Stopped at the session budget after spending $X.'

After a raise the next planning pass recomputes `limit` with the larger `budget_raised`, the guard passes, and the dropped spawn is emitted again (fixture asserts `spawn generate-spec spec#1` after the raise).

patterns.description: Every Step::Spawn passes through Planner::push. When ctx.budget_usd is Some, the planner compares state.spent_usd() with budget + state.budget_raised. At or above the limit it drops the spawn and, if no budget gate is open (state.budget_gate is None), pushes one OpenGate step with a BudgetReached payload. Only Step::Spawn is guarded: Judge, Command, Deliver, and OpenGate steps are not. The check uses >=, not >.
patterns.name: Budget guard inside Planner::push

patterns.description: SessionState::spent_usd sums usage.cost_usd over executions whose result is Some. Running executions are not counted until they finish. Judge cost is not included. The raise is also fold state (budget_raised), so the planner stays pure and a raise survives a restart.
patterns.name: Spend as a fold over finished executions

patterns.description: The runner reads the workspace limit fresh on every planning pass. A value of 0 or below becomes None, which disables the guard.

patterns.description: On any answer the fold clears budget_gate. A choice 'raise' parses text (trimmed, leading $ stripped) as a positive finite f64; otherwise the extra amount is budget_usd.max(1.0), where budget_usd is the limit recorded in the gate. budget_raised grows by extra plus any overshoot (spent_usd - budget_usd, floored at 0), so the new ceiling is spent plus extra. Any other answer, including 'stop', sets state.failed, which ends the session.
patterns.name: Gate answer folded in on_gate_answered

patterns.description: Planner::flows skips any open gate for which yolo_leaves_open is true, so no Step::YoloAnswer is emitted. document.problem: The workspace setting limits.session_budget_usd caps what one session spends. Enforcement is spread over four places: the fold sums spend and holds the raise, the planner turns a spawn into a gate, the runner answers and validates gates, and the YOLO code refuses to answer the gate. A change to this behavior has to touch each place consistently and update the fixture and docs page that pin it.

submit.findings_summary: The budget is enforced by the pure planner. In Planner::push (plan.rs), each Step::Spawn is compared with limit = ctx.budget_usd + state.budget_raised against SessionState::spent_usd(), which sums only finished executions and excludes judge cost. At or above the limit the spawn is dropped and one BudgetReached gate (stage Intake, kind budget_reached) opens if state.budget_gate is None. The user answers with a Choice: raise adds the typed dollars (default is the gate's limit, min 1) plus any overshoot to budget_raised, and any other choice sets state.failed. YOLO never answers it: Planner::flows skips it via yolo_leaves_open, and yolo_plan returns None. The conformance fixtures budget_pauses_spawns_until_raised and budget_stop_ends_the_session pin this, and docs/internals/spend-and-limits.md describes it.

data_flow.step: A planner rule decides a gate is needed. For BudgetReached it is Planner::push, which replaces a Spawn step with Step::OpenGate once state.spent_usd() >= ctx.budget_usd + state.budget_raised and state.budget_gate is None. Other kinds call Planner::gate(title, explanation, payload). Planner output is deduplicated by Step::key() = "gate:{kind_str}:{gate_owner}".

The runner's driver performs the step. perform() matches Step::OpenGate and appends SessionEvent::GateOpened { id: GateId::new(), title, explanation, payload } through Inner::append (store, fold, broadcast, wake). ImplementationReview first writes the session context file; no other kind has pre-open work.

Inner::append stores the event and folds it. SessionState::apply inserts a GateRecord (answer None) and calls on_gate_opened, which records the gate id in the owning track (budget_gate for BudgetReached).
The same append materializes the gate into the workspace db gates table (payload as JSON). No schema change is needed for a new variant.

The same append calls push_for (L1441 calls, L1489 defines). For a GateOpened event it returns early with no notice when the session is YOLO and the payload is not HarnessFailure (L1494). BudgetReached is a gate YOLO leaves open, yet a YOLO session gets no push for it, which differs from docs/internals/spend-and-limits.md ("With push notifications on, the open gate sends one"). A non-YOLO gate gets the generic body "A step is waiting for your decision." unless it is HarnessFailure or Permission, which have their own body.

The server sends GateView { id, session, title, explanation, payload, answer, source, reason, opened_at, answered_at } over REST and WebSocket. view.rs derives the waiting label from payload.stage().lane() (L83-84) and PendingGate.kind from payload.kind_str() (L978); the activity feed in ostra-server/src/nav/activity.rs uses kind_str() too.

The console renders it: GateCard.OpenForm checks isChoiceKind(p.kind) (ANSWER_KIND[kind] === "choice"), then ChoiceGate renders body(payload), the optional text field, and one Button per CHOICES[kind] entry. A click calls choiceAnswer (checks required text, and for budget raise parses dollars) and submits { kind: "choice", option, text } with api.answerGate(gate.id, { answer }).

Under YOLO, instead, Planner::flows emits Step::YoloAnswer for the open gate unless it is Permission or yolo_leaves_open; perform_yolo calls yolo_plan and appends GateAnswered with source Yolo for a Fixed plan, or calls the YOLO-answer judge for a Judge plan. A None plan returns without doing anything.

Runner::answer_gate loads the gate row, rejects an already answered gate, runs validate_answer(payload, answer) (shape plus per-kind content checks), then appends GateAnswered { id, source: User, answer, reason: None, routed: answer_needs_route(payload, answer) }.

The fold applies GateAnswered once (ignores an unknown or already answered gate), stores the answer on the GateRecord, then on_gate_answered clears the track's gate id and updates state (budget_raised grows on raise; failed is set on stop). The next next_steps call sees the new state and the planner resumes, here by emitting the spawn it had held back.
The answered card in the console is DesignGateCard with answerSummary(gate), which uses the CHOICES label of the chosen option.

patterns.description: A gate is one variant of the serde-tagged enum GatePayload (tag "kind", snake_case, ts-rs exported). Both stage() and kind_str() are exhaustive matches, so a missing arm is a compile error. kind_str() is the string the web, the store views, PendingGate, Step::summary(), Step::key(), and conformance fixtures use. stage() chooses the StageKind (and so the lane) shown for the open gate. The doc comment on the variant states the answers. The variant is placed last so the generated TypeScript union and serialized order stay stable.
patterns.name: GatePayload variant with stage() and kind_str() arms

patterns.description: on_gate_opened stores the new gate id in the track the gate belongs to (for BudgetReached, SessionState::budget_gate), so the planner can tell the gate is already open and does not emit it twice. on_gate_answered clears that id and applies the answer as state change. Both are exhaustive over GatePayload. For a Choice answer, `choice` is (option, text trimmed and empty filtered); any option string that is not matched falls into the `_` arm, which for BudgetReached means stop. The fold reads only the event and the payload (pure); the raise parses `text` in the fold, so the validation of the amount is client-side only. A fact from outside the log must be recorded in the event (CLAUDE.md pattern 1).
patterns.name: Fold: record the open gate, apply the answer

patterns.description: Planner rules call self.gate(title, explanation, payload) or push Step::OpenGate directly. push() deduplicates on Step::key(), which for a gate is "gate:{kind_str}:{gate_owner(payload)}". gate_owner is an exhaustive match that returns the identity of the thing the gate is about (the phase, execution, project, round, or an empty string for a per-session singleton like BudgetReached). The planner must not re-emit a gate that is already open: the budget rule checks `self.s.budget_gate.is_none()` (fold state set by on_gate_opened). Settings reach the planner only through PlanCtx (budget_usd), set in Runner::plan_ctx from workspace limits.
patterns.name: Planner opens a gate through push(), keyed by kind and owner

patterns.description: Planner::flows pushes Step::YoloAnswer for every open gate except Permission and any gate for which yolo_leaves_open is true. Then perform_yolo calls yolo_plan, an exhaustive match that returns Fixed (a fixed GateAnswer with a reason), Judge (a JSON schema for the YOLO-answer judge, whose output goes through yolo_answer_from_judge), or None (nothing happens). A gate YOLO must not answer needs both: add it to yolo_leaves_open so the planner emits no step, and return None in yolo_plan (the arm is required by exhaustiveness anyway). docs/internals/spend-and-limits.md says the rule is enforced in two places for this reason. A Judge plan additionally needs a branch in yolo_answer_from_judge, whose wildcard returns an error ("this gate is answered without the judge") and so makes a YOLO Judge gate wait for the user with a Note.
patterns.name: YOLO decision is made in two places

patterns.description: validate_answer pairs each payload with the GateAnswer variants it accepts in one matches! expression. It is not an exhaustive match: a payload missing from it compiles and then every answer is refused with "That answer does not fit this gate." at run time. All Choice gates are listed in one or-pattern. Per-kind content checks follow as separate if-let blocks (open questions all answered; spec/plan rejection needs feedback; ImplementationReview option must be done or feedback with text). BudgetReached has no content check: any option string and any text is accepted, and the fold treats anything other than raise as stop. The web mirrors the shape check in ANSWER_KIND and the content checks in choiceAnswer.
patterns.name: validate_answer: shape check by matches! with a default of rejection

patterns.description: A gate answered by picking one option is added to the web in four hand-synchronized places: the ChoiceGateKind union and CHOICES entry in lib/gateAnswers.ts (option strings must equal what the fold matches; exactly one primary per kind, enforced by a test), a case in ChoiceGate.tsx body() (compiler-enforced because the switch has no default), an optional case in textField(), and the ANSWER_KIND entry (compiler-enforced by Record<GateKindName, AnswerKind>). GateCard.OpenForm routes by isChoiceKind, which reads ANSWER_KIND, so nothing else changes. A gate with a different answer shape (Questions, Approval, Closing, Permission, Skills) needs a new component and a case in GateCard.OpenForm; without one the default branch renders a card with no actions.
patterns.name: Web: Choice gate registry

patterns.description: A planner or fold change is tested with the H helper: build an event history, call h.open_gate(kind) to append the GateOpened the planner asked for, h.answer(...) to append GateAnswered, and compare h.summaries() with expected Step::summary() strings (for a gate, "gate {kind_str}"). The budget fixtures also set h.ctx.budget_usd and use spend() to add a finished execution with a cost. The YOLO case checks that no yolo-answer step is emitted.
patterns.name: Fixture per rule in tests/conformance

document.problem: CLAUDE.md gives a one-line recipe for a new gate kind: variant in GatePayload with stage() and kind_str() arms, fold in on_gate_opened and on_gate_answered, a planner step, a yolo_plan decision, a validate_answer arm, a fixture, and regenerated TypeScript. The recipe omits several places that either fail at compile time (exhaustive matches) or silently fail at run time (default-false matches, default fallbacks in the web). This document records every site, which are compiler-checked, and what the existing BudgetReached gate does at each, so a new kind can be added without missing one.
document.scope: Task: how a gate kind is added end to end: GatePayload, the fold, the planner, yolo_plan, validate_answer, TypeScript types, and the console's gate cards. Covers the Rust path from the enum to the answer fold, the generated TypeScript, the web gate cards, the design GateCard, the fixtures that test it, and the docs pages that list gate kinds. Uses the existing BudgetReached gate as the worked example. It does not design any specific new gate and does not cover the browser tests under tests/browser or the site.
document.title: Adding a gate kind end to end

submit.findings_summary: A gate kind is a GatePayload variant with exhaustive stage() and kind_str() arms. The fold records it in on_gate_opened and applies the answer in on_gate_answered. The planner opens it through Planner::push or Planner::gate, deduplicated by Step::key() via gate_owner. judge_input::yolo_plan and yolo_leaves_open decide the YOLO handling, and the shape of the answer is checked in runner::validate_answer. Several sites are not compiler-checked: validate_answer and answer_needs_route use default-reject or default-false matches, the web OpenForm default renders a card with no buttons, and the hand-written ChoiceGateKind and design GateKind unions. The TypeScript in web/src/api/gen is regenerated by cargo test -p ostra-core through TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR. The web side needs ANSWER_KIND, CHOICES, ChoiceGate body and textField, mock fixtures, and gateAnswers.test.ts, which pins the full maps. Two drift findings: runner push_for sends no push for any gate in a YOLO session except HarnessFailure, contradicting docs/internals/spend-and-limits.md, and the design GateKind lacks implementation_review.
